constraints: Read selected regular members of a locally built gzip tar archive without extraction; reject duplicate/missing/type/size/content mismatches against trusted checkout inputs.
Finite consumer inventory and static package prefix; this is not hostile-archive handling, dependency closure or a release signature validator.
alternatives: Python tarfile plus the current setuptools file-selection engine gives direct entry inspection and a check of actual manifest selection semantics.
Java/Kotlin Apache Commons Compress and C#/F# System.Formats.Tar provide credible independent archive readers; Hatch file selection is an alternative packaging design.
rationale: KEEP Python inspection and existing manifest selection: six synthetic archive methods and one finite manifest method pass; no archive extraction or local distribution build performed.

Other readers do not eliminate the need to inspect actual build selection. No throughput requirement, demonstrated resource failure or measured alternative advantage justifies a migration in this trusted developer-tool boundary.
limits: Official-source candidate comparison only; no alternative executable or speed benchmark.
Local focused source tests only; no new installed distribution, hosted matrix, P19 customer acceptance, physical, hard-real-time, MLS/CNSA or availability claim.
